findings.evidence: template/scripts/lifecycle_workers.py `login_preflight` loops over all `job["providers"]` and raises on the first failure. `job_eligible` (line 345-351) accepts a job when `set(named) & set(ready)` is non-empty. pr_review_gate.py:327-329 then filters `review_config["providers"]` to `review_ready`. For a job naming [claude, codex] where only codex has a login, the worker exits non-zero before claiming. The same job is re-selected on each run, so it keeps failing.
findings.summary: The pre-claim login preflight requires every provider named by the job to log in. Eligibility and execution only need the ready subset, so one unbound provider can block a job that could have run.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/pr_review_gate.py:534-537 and template/scripts/requirement_composition.py:555-558 both use `provider = "claude" if claude_binary is not None and argv[0] == claude_binary else "codex"`. `bound_preflight` in independent_review_runner.py builds a separate `providers_by_binary` map. If binary resolution differs between calls, or a symlinked or relative argv[0] is used, the claude token is silently dropped. A KeyError is also possible in `bound_launcher`.
findings.summary: The default launchers infer the provider by comparing argv[0] to the resolved claude binary, and treat everything else as codex. This is fragile and duplicated in two places.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/lifecycle_workers.py `read_login_token`: `for parent in path.resolve().parents: if (parent / ".git").exists(): raise`. The error names the parent directory but gives no way to override.
findings.summary: The 'outside any git checkout' rule walks all parents for a `.git` entry. A token file anywhere under a home directory that is itself a git repo (a dotfiles repo in `~`) is rejected.
